items: ~3 years ago it was clear AI would transform software engineering
Built tools to automate programming aspects early on

slides.notes: Personal journey into AI-assisted coding. Mechatyper was an early experiment in automating code writing.

elements.Text: The most important concept in programming is the function — not the class, module, or file.

items: Design data types first (small footprint, many dependencies)

slides.notes: This methodology came from trying to make AI code generation work better. Bottom-up tree traversal of atomic code units produces the best AI-generated code quality (confirmed by Mantle engineering).

elements.Text: AI without constraints creates files it doesn't want to use as context. There is nothing better for AI than reading a file name and knowing what's inside.

slides.notes: Claude Code exhibits a 165:1 read-to-write token ratio. A single whitespace difference between the AI's expectation and actual code results in a failed edit, triggering expensive retry loops.

items: If it compiles, a whole class of bugs is gone

slides.notes: The compiler is the harness (Adam Benenson). The type system reduces ambiguity for AI. GitHub confirmed in 2025: AI is pushing developers toward typed languages. TypeScript overtook Python and JavaScript as most-used language on GitHub.

elements.Text: If we have functions and data structures forming a graph — why do we need files?

items: AI coding assistants use files wrong
They don't use AST — they use line search and complex text edits
Files are a human serialization format, not a natural unit of code
First transition: split files into smallest possible atoms

slides.notes: The key insight. I write production Rust as if files were graph nodes: functions and data structures are separate, avoiding syntactic sugar like proc macros. When I'm lazy and don't include these guidelines, I regret it.
Transition slide. The fileless idea has deep roots going back to the 1970s.

Smalltalk: live objects in memory images, Alan Kay called it 'a recursion on the notion of computer itself'. Unison: names are just metadata pointers, renaming never breaks anything, builds are unnecessary. Dark: edit = deploy, $3.5M funding, ran out of money but storage model is still relevant. Lamdu: 'no files, folders or line numbers, no merge conflicts on renaming'. SpacetimeDB: written in Rust, powers an entire MMORPG (BitCraft Online).

Quote.author: Malte Skarupke, 2014
Quote.text: I think there is a global maximum out there that does not involve text files, but we keep discovering that we're not at the local maximum for text files yet.

slides.notes: This quote perfectly captures the situation. We keep optimizing file-based workflows instead of questioning the premise. Kiro's AST-based editing is still optimizing within the file paradigm.

elements.Text: Kiro (AWS, Feb 2026) — first mainstream AST-based AI editing
But Kiro still operates on files. What if storage were also graph-native?

slides.notes: Kiro uses structural selectors like ClassName.methodName with typed operations: insert_node, replace_node, delete_node. Formatting changes don't break edits. This validates the thesis but doesn't go far enough.

elements.Text: Inspired by Crux — Core (pure Rust logic) + Shell (platform I/O)

Quote.author: Ian Bull
Quote.text: The architecture is the prompt. The structure of your code is the most important instruction you give to the AI.

slides.notes: Capabilities decompose platform-dependent side effects. If your system is built from sinks (not pipes), AI can reason about components in isolation. Pure functions align with LLMs' stateless nature. Rust already has an effect system: async, const, ?, unsafe.

elements.Text: A self-contained environment where apps are nothing but:

items: TEA architecture: Model / Msg / init / update / view
MCP as the primary development interface

slides.notes: Core architecture overview. No files, no filesystem. Functions and types stored in a database, addressed by content hash. Name pointers can be atomically updated.

Quote.author: Mykhailo Chalyi
Quote.text: I stopped using third-party libraries for API calls. I ask my coding agent to generate a client library specifically for the APIs I need.

items: Why import a library for one function when AI can rewrite it?
Zero-dependency code leaves the model room to think
The system assimilates functionality rather than importing it

slides.notes: This pattern is emerging naturally. Dawid Prus: 'Zero-dependency libraries leave the model room to think. Dependency stacks fill it with noise.' The process begins with 'I don't want to import another dependency' and ends with 'I guess I accidentally built one.'

items: Systems fully managed by AI agent swarms
Self-healing: 71% of incidents resolved without humans (avg 4.7 min)
No versions, no releases — continuous development, immediate deployment
The graph is the file system
The compiler is the test suite

slides.notes: Think of something and work backwards to achieve it. A swarm of AI agents constantly improving every aspect: speed, security, functionality. Current self-healing systems resolve incidents in 4.7 minutes vs 76.2 minutes manually.
